notes: §1985:IV.4.2.2.2.1.3 GR1: "The value of a nonnumeric literal in the object program is the value represented by character-1." The lexer token STRINGLIT carries the literal as written; CobolLiteral.Decode (through SplitLiteral) removes the two delimiters and collapses each doubled quotation mark to one (§1985:IV.4.2.2.2.1.2 SR2) and changes no other character, ExpressionBinder.NonNumericLiteralOperand binds that text as the operand of a statement and ValueInitializer.InitializerFrom as a VALUE, and EmitText.CsLiteral (EmitCore.cs) writes it into the C# through Roslyn SymbolDisplay.FormatLiteral, so a backslash, a brace or a quotation mark in the value cannot change in the emitted program. The path has no edition arm, so --std 85 reaches it as every edition does; the one 2023 addition, the zero-length literal, is refused at 85 (COBOL0900). Probed at --std 85 (l1.cob): case, single and repeated spaces, leading and trailing spaces, doubled quotation marks, backslash sequences, {0}, "*>", "==" and a literal continued over two lines are each the written characters in DISPLAY, MOVE, VALUE, STRING (whose POINTER counts them) and a comparison ("abc" is not equal to "ABC"). The witness displays "ABC  XYZ" and moves "AB-12 Z." to a PIC X(8) item.

next.reason: 1985: "The value of a nonnumeric literal in the object program is the value represented by character-1."; 2023: "If character-1 is not specified, the literal is a zero-length literal. ... the implementor shall specify the applicable general rules.". 2023 keeps the value as character-1 converted to runtime. It adds a zero-length literal case and leaves UTF-8 or mixed content to implementor-specified rules; neither appears in 1985.
